title: Welding Safety Checklist (29 CFR 1910.252)
subtitle: Use before hot work starts and while welding, cutting or brazing is under way.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item is marked Defect, do not start or continue the hot work until it is corrected, and record what was done.
The equipment manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Area preparation and authorization
items: The authorizing person has inspected the area and named the precautions before work begins
Combustibles at least 35 feet from the work, or, where moving them is impracticable, under flameproofed covers or behind metal guards or curtains
Floor clear of paper clippings, wood shavings, textile fibers and similar combustibles for 35 feet around the work
Cracks, floor openings, wall holes, open doorways and broken windows closed or protected so sparks cannot reach combustibles beyond them
Ducts and conveyors that could carry sparks to distant combustibles are protected or shut down
In a sprinklered building, sprinkler protection is not impaired
No flammable gas, vapor, liquid or dust mixtures with air at the work, and no accumulation of combustible dust
Used drums, barrels or tanks cleaned of flammables, greases, tars and acids before hot work
Extinguishers, hose, water pails or sand buckets suited to the combustibles present, ready for instant use
Combustibles behind a metal wall, partition, ceiling or roof relocated, or a fire watch posted on that side

sections.title: Fire watch and training
items: A fire watcher is assigned where more than a minor fire could develop or a condition in 1910.252(a)(2)(iii)(A) applies, such as combustibles within 35 feet
Fire watcher has an extinguisher or other firefighting equipment within reach and has been trained to use it
Fire watcher knows where and how to raise the alarm
Fire watch continues for at least a half hour after hot work ends
Cutters, welders and their supervisors can show training in safe operation of the equipment and process
Firefighting equipment is properly located at the site

sections.title: Eye, face and body protection
items: Each arc welder or arc cutter uses a helmet or hand shield (submerged arc welding excluded)
Helpers and attendants wear proper eye protection
Gas welders and oxygen cutters wear goggles or other suitable eye protection
Lenses carry a permanent mark showing source and shade
Where the work permits, the welder works inside a booth or noncombustible screens with a low-reflectivity finish
Air can move freely under or through booths and screens at floor level
People next to the welding area are behind noncombustible or flameproof screens or shields, or wear appropriate goggles
Protective clothing and other PPE selected under 1910.132 for the size, nature and location of the job
Welders and helpers on platforms, scaffolds or runways are protected by railings, safety belts, life lines or an equally effective safeguard
Welding cable and equipment kept out of passageways and off ladders and stairways

sections.title: Ventilation, fumes and hazard communication
items: Exhaust or general ventilation running and positioned so toxic fumes, gases and dusts stay below the 1910.1000 limits
Mechanical ventilation provided in spaces under 10,000 cubic feet per welder, under a 16-foot ceiling, or with obstructed cross ventilation
Movable hood placed as near as practicable to the work
Chlorinated hydrocarbon degreasing located so its vapors cannot reach the welding atmosphere
Lead-bearing metals and lead paint worked indoors only with local exhaust ventilation or airline respirators running
Workers can reach the labels and safety data sheets for the fluxes, filler metals and coatings in use
Filler metal and fusible granular material containers carry the ventilation warning notice
First-aid equipment on hand during all work

sections.title: Confined spaces and containers
items: Gas cylinders and welding machines are outside the confined space
Heavy wheeled portable equipment securely blocked before work starts
A way to pull the welder out quickly is in place, and any lifeline is attached so the body cannot jam in the opening
Attendant stationed outside, watching the welder continuously, with a preplanned rescue procedure
Space ventilated, and replacement air is clean and respirable
Oxygen is not being used to ventilate the space
During long breaks in arc welding, electrodes are out of holders, holders placed safely and the machine disconnected
During long breaks, torch valves closed and fuel-gas and oxygen shut off at a point outside the space
Hollow spaces, cavities and containers vented to let air or gases escape before preheating, cutting or welding
Hot metal marked or another warning given to other workers after welding

references: 29 CFR 1910.252: General requirements (Part 1910 Subpart Q: Welding, Cutting and Brazing)
